notes.claim: The conjugate of a + bi is a - bi: the same number with the sign of the imaginary part changed.
On the plane the conjugate is the mirror image of the number in the real axis.
A complex number times its conjugate is a real number.
Division is done by multiplying numerator and denominator by the complex conjugate of the denominator.

sources.title: Algebra - Complex Numbers — Lamar University
sources.quote: The conjugate of the complex number (a + bi) is the complex number (a - bi). In other words, it is the original complex number with the sign on the imaginary part changed.

sources.title: 2.4 Complex Numbers - College Algebra 2e | OpenStax
sources.quote: When a complex number is multiplied by its complex conjugate, the result is a real number.

sources.title: Week 4 – Complex Numbers — University of Oxford, Mathematical Institute
sources.quote: Note that the conjugate z of a point z is its mirror image in the real axis.

sources.title: HIGHER ENGINEERING MATHEMATICS — Higher Engineering Mathematics (Bird)
sources.quote: (iii) Division of complex numbers is achieved by multiplying both numerator and denominator by the complex conjugate of the denominator.
